text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple 5xx and timeout spikes detected for org="sylphnet" starting ~1788888800. Error-rate rising, request latency > 2.5s, some customers hitting retries. Auto-mitigation not triggered (policy threshold mismatch).

oncall-neo: I'm paging SRE. Looking at dashboards now. Can someone confirm customer-visible failures?

cs-omar: SylphNet support thread reporting ~30% of requests failing, retries causing billing webhook backlog. High priority for CS.

sre-alyssa: I see a sharp QPS increase from one API key for sylphnet; sustained burst ~3x normal. Their org-level RL is 2000 qps. Token and model latencies also spiking.

eng-runtime-jun: We should do an emergency org-level RL bump + disable heavy rerank path for that org to reduce tokens. We can toggle via admin API: `POST /internal/orgs/sylphnet/ops/rate-limit` or use opsctl.

oncall-neo: Proposed plan: 1) Temp increase org rate limit to 4500 qps for 3 hours, 2) Toggle off `rerank.v2` feature flag for org, 3) Watch 15m windows, roll back to 2200 if stable. Who can execute?

sre-alyssa: I can run the RL change. I'll also create a monitor with tighter alerting. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/org-rate-mitigation

eng-runtime-jun: Command I'd use (internal):
```
opsctl org-rate update --org sylphnet --qps 4500 --ttl 3h --reason "emergency bump due to spike (auto-monitor)"
```
and
```
ffctl set --org sylphnet --flag rerank_v2 false --reason "emergency reduce token use"
```

incident-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: oncall-neo to acknowledge and run ops steps or confirm SRE will.

oncall-neo: Acknowledged. Running now. Will post command output.

oncall-neo: (run) `opsctl org-rate update --org sylphnet --qps 4500 --ttl 3h --note "inc 1788888888 emergency bump"`
oncall-neo: Command result: OK -> org=sylphnet qps=4500 ttl=10800s id=rl-99321

oncall-neo: (run) `ffctl set --org sylphnet --flag rerank_v2 false`
oncall-neo: Command result: OK -> feature=rerrank_v2 disabled for org=sylphnet

sre-alyssa: Monitor warming up. Within 5m: 5xx down from 28% -> 6%, p95 latency falling to 900ms. Good sign.

cs-omar: SylphNet support reporting immediate reduction in failed requests, still seeing some webhook backlog but overall better.

product-zoe: Heads-up: feature flag toggle may affect ranking quality for a subset of flows; CS notified. We'll need a customer note if we keep extended.

sre-alyssa: Creating incident ticket: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-4317 (owner: oncall-neo). Tagging for postmortem.

oncall-neo: Setting slack reminder to check at +2h and to roll down if stable. ` /remind #incidents in 2 hours to evaluate sylphnet RL`

incident-bot: MONITOR: 30m window looks stable, error-rate ~3%, latency p95 ~850ms.

oncall-neo: Rolling RL back to 2200 qps now per plan. `opsctl org-rate update --org sylphnet --qps 2200 --note "planned rollback after stabilization"` -> OK id=rl-99322

sre-alyssa: Re-enabled rerank flag? We should turn it back on only after verifying token usage is healthy.

oncall-neo: Re-enabled `rerank_v2` via `ffctl set --org sylphnet --flag rerank_v2 true` -> OK

cs-omar: Customer-facing summary: "We briefly increased your request throughput and disabled experimental reranking to mitigate a surge that caused partial failures. Services returned to normal; we're following up with root cause and mitigation details." I'll draft and send.

product-zoe: Postmortem owner?

sre-alyssa: I'll take postmortem. CS owns customer comms. Add notes: spike source API key, consider quota guardrails and alert tuning to auto-trigger.

oncall-neo: Closing thread for live mitigation. Will keep incident ticket open until postmortem complete. :white_check_mark:
